facts.statement: The genus Prophaethon was first described by Andrews in 1899.
Prophaethon was an extinct seabird that lived during the Early Eocene, approximately 56 to 49 million years ago.
facts.quote: Prophaethon is an extinct genus of seabird that lived during the Early Eocene (Ypresian, c.56-49 mya)

facts.statement: Prophaethon is classified as a distant relative of tropicbirds.
facts.quote: As indicated by its generic name, it is a distant relative of the tropicbirds.

facts.statement: The type species P. shrubsolei is known from a holotype consisting of a skull and some limb bones.
facts.quote: The type species, P. shrubsolei, is essentially known from a holotype specimen consisting of fairly comprehensive fossil remains of a single individual, namely a skull and some limb bones

facts.statement: The holotype remains of P. shrubsolei were recovered from the London Clay on the Isle of Sheppey, England.
facts.quote: which were recovered from the London Clay on the Isle of Sheppey, England

facts.statement: Gerald Mayr described additional remains of P. shrubsolei found at Walton-on-the-Naze in the London Clay.
facts.quote: more remains of P. shrubsolei were described by Gerald Mayr, having been found at Walton-on-the-Naze, also in the London Clay

facts.statement: A second species, P. waltonensis, was described from fossil remains found at Walton-on-the-Naze.
facts.quote: A second species, P. waltonensis, has also been described from fossil remains hailing from Walton-on-the-Naze

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Prophaethon is Prophaethontidae.
Prophaethon belongs to the family Prophaethontidae.
The time range for Prophaethon spans from the Thanetian to the Ypresian, between 59.24 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Ypresian (59.24 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Prophaethon is classified in the class Aves.
